intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: From the first 10 m telescope (the upgraded CANGAROO-II); the end is the 2011 stop of CANGAROO activities.
intervals.quote: The first telescope of this array is the upgraded version of the CANGAROO-II 7 m telescope and has been in operation since March 2000.

intervals.label: observing activities ended
intervals.quote: Eventually, the activities in Australia were stopped in 2011.

name: CANGAROO-III telescope array
notes: The first telescope T1 (the former CANGAROO-II) was not in use at the time of the 2007 observations (arXiv:0908.1610).

placements.note: Start is the first 10 m telescope (March 2000); site-level coordinate only.
placements.quote: The CANGAROO-III imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope system which consists of four telescopes are operated in Woomera

energy_range.quote: CANGAROO-III is an Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (IACT) array of four 10 m telescopes for very high energy (sub-TeV) gamma-ray astronomy.

telescope_count.quote: The CANGAROO-III imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope system which consists of four telescopes are operated in Woomera

summary.plain: Four 10 metre telescopes standing at the corners of a diamond in the Australian outback, each with a camera that photographs the flash of light from a gamma-ray air shower.
summary.technical: Four 10 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (114 FRP mirror segments, 57.3 m2, 427-pixel cameras) arranged in a diamond; first telescope the upgraded CANGAROO-II (March 2000), T1 later out of use.

technology.quote: Each reflector consists of 114 small spherical mirrors of 80 cm diameter, which are made of Fiber Reinforced Plastic
technology.value: Four 10 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, each a parabolic reflector of 114 small spherical FRP mirrors of 80 cm diameter.
